## Quick context

This repository implements a small RAG-based insight agent with three primary entry points:
- `rag_setup.py` — build / update FAISS vectorstore from PDFs and a sales CSV (embeddings, chunking, dedup manifest).
- `rag_agent.py` — LangGraph-based agent: typed `State`, nodes (type analysis, pdf/sales analysis, chart, recommend) and orchestration.
- `rag_app.py` — Streamlit UI that wires a `rag_chain` into a user-facing chat and evaluation panels.

Key directories and files to reference: `prompts/` (prompt templates), `data/` (sales csv + extracted summary), `eval_data/` (testcases), `utils/` (prompt & line loaders, JSON cleaning), and `logging_config.py`.

## What you need to know to be productive

- Environment & startup:
  - The project reads many settings from `.env` (see `rag_setup.py`). Important vars: `MODEL_DEFAULT`, `MODEL_TEMPERATURE`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `FAISS_INDEX_PATH`, `EVAL_TEST_DATA_FILE_PATH`, and `PDFS` (a JSON string).
  - Typical workflow: install deps -> `python rag_setup.py` to (re)build the RAG index -> `python rag_eval.py` to run tests -> `streamlit run rag_app.py` to open the UI.

- Prompt loading pattern:
  - Prompts are loaded via `utils/prompt_loader.py` using the key name (e.g. `RECOMMENDATION_PROMPT`) or `*_PATH` env var pointing at files in `prompts/`.
  - `load_prompt` uses an LRU cache; if you change prompt files in development call `load_prompt.cache_clear()` before invoking flows so the code reloads them.
  - Files may include a CUTOFF_MARKER line to ignore trailing content.

- Vectorstore & dedup:
  - FAISS index path is built as `${FAISS_INDEX_PATH_BASE}_${model}` (see `rag_setup.py`). The manifest `.faiss_manifest.txt` is used to avoid duplicate chunks.
  - Stable chunk ids are generated by `generate_doc_id(content, metadata)` using SHA256 of content+selected metadata — preserve that if you change chunking.

- Document types and routing:
  - Documents set `metadata['type']` to either `pdf` or `sales_summary`. The agent's `type_analysis_node` calls `test_retrieval_only()` and decides routing based on counts of these types.
  - Sales summaries are created in `create_sales_sumry()` (see `rag_setup.py`) and stored as `Document` objects with metadata fields like `month`, `product`, `total_sales`, `avg_satisfaction`.

- LLM + embeddings mapping:
  - `create_embeds_genrtr(model)` maps model names to embedding providers (Ollama/GG/OpenAI). Keep mappings synchronized if you add new models.
  - The agent prefixes messages with a model/temperature tag like: `[model, temp] - <query>`; several tests/cleanups strip this prefix (see `rag_eval.py`).

## Developer workflows & useful commands

- Setup virtualenv and install:
  - python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
- Rebuild the RAG index (deletes/creates index based on env flags):
  - python rag_setup.py
- Run full evaluation pipeline (loads test set, runs agent, evaluates with QAEvalChain):
  - python rag_eval.py
- Run the interactive UI:
  - streamlit run rag_app.py

## Project-specific conventions and gotchas

- Prompts are accessed by keys used throughout codebase: examples include `PDF_TYPE_PROMPT`, `SALES_DATA_ANALYSIS_PROMPT`, `CHART_PROMPT`, `RECOMMENDATION_PROMPT`, and `EVAL_PROMPT`. Look in `prompts/` for canonical examples.
- Prompt loader supports either file-path env variables (e.g. `RECOMMENDATION_PROMPT_PATH=prompts/recommendation_prompt.txt`) or direct env values (`RECOMMENDATION_PROMPT=`).
- `RECREATE_VECTORSTORE` default behavior can remove the existing FAISS folder; check `rag_setup.py` before running if you want to preserve an index.
- The Streamlit UI stores the selected model & chunking params in `st.session_state`. Changing the model via the UI recreates the rag_chain and replaces `st.session_state.rag_chain`.

## Integration points to be careful with

- External services: OpenAI, Google GenAI, and Ollama (embeddings/llm). Keys are read from env and failing configs will raise early in `rag_setup.py` when creating embeddings/LLMs.
- FAISS disk paths and manifests: concurrent runs that both write to the same FAISS directory may corrupt the index — prefer single-process operations for indexing.

## Where to look for examples

- RAG-only retrieval example: `test_retrieval_only()` in `rag_setup.py` (useful for debugging what the retriever returns before invoking the LLM).
- End-to-end eval: `run_full_eval()` in `rag_eval.py` shows creating a `rag_chain`, building an agent, running tests, and evaluating.
- Chart rendering contract: `chart_node()` in `rag_agent.py` expects the LLM to return JSON with `chart_type`, `chart_data`, and `summary` (the code uses `clean_json_string()` then `json.loads()`).

If any of these sections are unclear or you'd like more examples (e.g. a minimal reproducer showing how prompts map to retrieved docs), tell me which area to expand and I will iterate.
